item.title: Re: Update
item.content:encoded:
In this case, think of Telekill as a token unit used for online in-game purchases.

You know, where a game has an in-game and/or online store that requires a unit of currency that almost never drops in-game (if it drops at all) but can be purchased if you're shelling out real-world money.

This article is using TELEKILL like that. Note the caps; that's what differentiates it from "telekill"/148. I'd personally use a different token name (ApollyonBucks, SCriP, MC&Dollars) to prevent that kind of mixup from readers. Then agsin, it may be intentional as another potshot at EA's Microtransactions that they don't care if the name is potentially confusing.

item.title: Re: Really?
item.content:encoded:
It's a circlejerk regardless of whether you agree with it. I think microtransactions are exploitative and bad, but I have to admit that people who agree with me about that are circlejerking.

I can easily see why someone would look at this article and come away with the impression that it's getting upvoted on the strength of that circlejerk. Circlejerks inflate the reception of underwhelming one-note content, which it's perfectly reasonable to describe this as.

Sure, 'circlejerk' isn't the nicest term that could be applied here, but it does kinda cut to the heart of the issue.

item.title: Re: Really?
item.content:encoded:
There's a way to find something unfunny beyond just calling insulting it with the term "circlejerk".

As to the two others, they're a joke reference to 148 and threat level that's mostly used in SCPs to make it stand out and get the audience invested (even if you find them stupid, which is a legitimate opinion to have). The latter's inclusion is meant to get the audience invested and then knock it down by hiding the important bits behind a paywall.
